transcript.question: Could you walk me through your background, your core technical strengths, and what motivated you to pursue this role?
transcript.answer_text: Um, I have been working in software engineering for three years, actually focusing on cloud services and APIs. I like building reliable systems with Python and AWS, and basically wanted to tackle larger scale distributed architectures at your company.

transcript.question: Describe a situation where you had a technical disagreement with a teammate or lead. How did you resolve it?
transcript.answer_text: We had a disagreement on whether to use DynamoDB or PostgreSQL for our session store. My teammate wanted relational, but I proposed DynamoDB because of predictable sub-millisecond latency. To resolve it objectively, we benchmarked both under simulated concurrency, reviewed the access patterns together, and agreed on DynamoDB. It resulted in zero scaling bottlenecks during peak traffic.

transcript.question: Imagine your service crashed during peak production traffic and customer data is potentially inconsistent. Walk me through your first 15 minutes of triage.
transcript.answer_text: Well, you know, it was really chaotic. I like quickly checked the logs and basically rolled back the last deployment immediately to prevent further errors. Then I verified database consistency.
